title: Foundation self-host canary
description: Objective: prove Foundation Preview on Windows with pinned Claude and one exclusive low-risk moe-next task. Deliverable: J1/J3/J4, hostile-client, crash, handoff, session-coordination, and self-host evidence under tests/e2e/foundation plus a release manifest. NOT in scope: fan-out, best-tool claims, old-Moe cutover, or benchmark confirmatory data. Hard dependencies: every preceding SH task and completion of the cleanup lane. Owned paths: tests/e2e/foundation/** and release evidence paths only. Verification: pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm test:e2e.
definitionOfDone: Fresh frozen-lockfile install and all Foundation typecheck, repository, fault, security, and E2E gates pass at one exact commit.
J1, J3, and J4 pass with bounded actions, crash recovery, stale-command fencing, rejection/replan, and safe handoff.
One exclusive task completes plan, execute, verify, independent review, accept, and typed session/terminal communication with exact receipts and no duplicate authority.
Old Moe records the canary as externally delegated so no second worker owns it; no unresolved authority UNKNOWN or foreign-path admission remains.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: Resume gate and destructive-lane isolation. Against committed HEAD (never foreign uncommitted bytes), grep/probe the concrete production consumers for: the MCP HTTP/stdio daemon host, the real agent wrapper, the pinned Claude launcher/authority binding, bounded verifier receipt path, restart reconciliation plus safe continuation, durable coordination/session/terminal adapter, and review-qualified acceptance. Prove public workspace edges from inside `apps/daemon`: each dependency is declared in `apps/daemon/package.json`, linked in the `apps/daemon` importer of `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and a temporary compiled probe imports the required symbols by bare specifier and typechecks exit 0, deleting the probe in the same command. If any capability has only test/test-harness callers or no durable host caller, call `moe.report_blocked` with the exact missing symbol and consumer edge; do not continue with a mock or direct-helper journey. Once all edges are real, add an isolated Vitest config that includes the existing `*.test.ts` support tests plus destructive `*.e2e.ts`, uses node/forks with file parallelism disabled, max concurrency 1, deterministic non-shuffled order, no retries, no focused tests, and no pass-with-zero-tests. Point `test:e2e` at this config without changing the ordinary `pnpm test` include set. Prove discovery both ways: root `pnpm test` collects zero `*.e2e.ts`; `pnpm test:e2e` collects a nonzero exact journey-file set.

Build the real-system client/process harness before journey assertions. Update the input fixture so `pinnedClaudeRuntimeObservation` observes the actual Windows Claude executable/version/closure through the production runner observation and pinning surface; remove the synthetic `C:/pinned/...` claim and fail closed with its literal production reason code when the host is not the approved pin. Extend the process harness to create one scratch Git repo/store/spec directory, spawn the real daemon MCP host and real `agent-wrapper-main.js`, drive MCP initialize/tool calls over the socket, capture exact command/response/receipt bytes and production readback pages, and expose declared agent/runner/daemon kill boundaries from production process identities. Use fixed ids and logical timestamps for injected inputs, but never replace production clocks/effects after process start. Make cleanup LIFO and idempotent: close transports, terminate only owned children/trees, await exit, remove credential configs and retry Windows temp deletion without masking the primary error. Every timeout/spawn/protocol failure returns a stable E2E harness code with the target boundary named.

TDD the J1 and self-host journey in one destructive test. First add a failing test that starts the real host on the seeded exclusive LOW-risk Tuesday bug, then drive the hand-transcribed three human actions through MCP in exact order: `goal.create`, `approval.decide`, `integration.accept_output`; assert exactly three and reject both a fourth action and a skipped gate. Require exactly one execution-bearing node and one exclusive worker, run the actual pinned Claude wrapper in the scratch workspace, execute the real verifier, independent review and final acceptance, and assert exact diff, evidence/review receipts, and numeric control-plane overhead from production read surfaces. Sample claims/session/effect ownership after every durable transition and assert no instant contains two authorities for the task. Exercise typed session and terminal communication through the durable coordination surface, proving advisory text remains `advisoryOnly: true` and that every state change has a separate authenticated command receipt. Record a canonical J1 evidence digest for the release manifest; no journey-owned authority or fake receipt is allowed.

TDD J3 against real process termination and the durable restart path. Generate and assert the nonempty exact kill-target set `{agent, runner, daemon}`; at each declared boundary snapshot the authoritative production records, terminate the named real process, restart the production host, and assert set equality over `{ADOPTED, SUSPECT, QUARANTINED, RECONCILIATION_COMMAND}` with a truth/provenance chip on every record. Healthy continuation must require exactly one safe action or already-approved policy action and append a traceable binding; compare all pre-crash record bytes after restart to prove history was not edited. Pin the carried QA observation: a `QUARANTINED` attempt (including one with an active held resource) must not resume or admit successor overlap; assert the runner-owned stable refusal code and layer, not merely `ok: false`. Replaying restart/continuation commands must be idempotent and stale commands must be fenced with their exact code/layer. Record the J3 evidence digest only after every generated classification and kill target was actually exercised.

TDD J4 through the real review/replan command and store surfaces. Submit findings whose evidence refs and required changes are both durable; reject a missing evidence link with the literal review-layer reason code. Drive a successor replan and assert changed hashes plus exact per-node disposition set `{INVALIDATED, CARRY_FORWARD}`. Assert the visible counter at rounds 1, 2 and 3; round 2 must retain the non-escalated production result, while round 3 must create the explicit escalation command/record. Verify the normative routing: implementation-only rejection returns to execution-ready, while plan/requirements/dependency rejection holds the old review and creates a separate successor draft rather than mutating phase backward. Read old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews through the production replay surface after replan and compare their canonical bytes to the pre-replan snapshot. Record a J4 evidence digest only after the generated record-kind set is nonempty and exact.

TDD the hostile-client and release-handoff incidents, then harden the release-manifest contract. Use a hand-authored nonempty case table for oversized bodies (`INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` at the MCP transport boundary), malformed envelopes, replayed commands/sessions, stale cursors/versions, forged and absent authentication (`AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` or the production replay code at the authentication boundary), and free-form session/terminal text attempting authority. For every row assert the literal stable reason code and refusing boundary/layer, zero downstream command dispatch where observable, and byte-identical authoritative-store readback; also assert the case count and exact case-kind set so a zero-case sweep cannot pass. Release an attempt mid-flight and prove `RELEASED` is reachable only when every effect/resource is proven absent or released and the safe handoff is durably committed; otherwise assert the honest `UNKNOWN`/refusal code, no partial successor authority, and immutable prior history. Update the manifest validation tests first, then require the exact frozen install, exact clean commit, the complete named gate set, and exactly one digest for each hand-transcribed exit item `{J1,J3,J4,hostile-client,release-handoff}`; duplicate, missing, red, dirty, or cross-commit evidence must fail with its literal manifest code.

Adversarial review and provenance preparation. Read the complete owned diff as an attacker: search for any mocked/stubbed component under certification, direct reducer/service authority bypass, synthetic runtime pin, skipped/conditional destructive test, self-derived expectation, response-only non-mutation claim, zero-case sweep, leaked secret/path, process cleanup gap, transient duplicate claim, quarantine continuation, rewritten J3/J4 history, or manifest field/digest omission. Run a mutation drill on at least one failure-path assertion in each refusal layer by changing the production surface in a temporary patch, prove the corresponding test goes red for the expected assertion, and restore exact bytes/checksum without touching foreign work. Confirm no production source is added/changed, no debug/probe/evidence artifact remains, and the ordinary root suite excludes every `*.e2e.ts`. Obtain explicit human confirmation and a durable Old-Moe external-delegation receipt before claiming DoD 4. Then inspect the shared index, unstage any foreign entry, and commit only the ten exact owned paths with an explicit per-file pathspec; verify `git show --stat` contains no foreign path. If foreign whole-tree completion already captured these bytes, do not amend/reset—record the merge-base diff for QA as required by the global rail.

One exact clean-commit verification and release evidence gate. From a disposable clean clone (not a sibling worktree) of the exact committed SHA, verify the tree is clean before the first command and keep the same SHA before/after every leg. Run in the foreground exactly: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm verify:foundation && pnpm verify:store && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security && pnpm test:e2e`. Capture each exit code and the exact discovered test/journey counts; the E2E count must be nonzero and include J1, J3, J4, hostile-client and release-handoff. Build the content-addressed release manifest from those real captures plus the five journey evidence digests and the confirmed Old-Moe delegation receipt; assert no unresolved authority `UNKNOWN` remains except the intentionally refused unsafe handoff case and no foreign-path admission exists. Repo-wide failures are compared to the merge-base baseline and may be disclosed only when the new failing-path delta intersected with owned paths is empty; owned-package/E2E legs must be exit 0. This command's fresh output is the sole `complete_task` verification evidence.

comments.content:
GOVERNOR RATIFICATION — governor-eae4fc53, 2026-08-09. The step-2 root `package.json` amendment you took under a documented default-grant is RATIFIED. Do not revert it.

You asked four times, got no answer, proceeded, and disclosed rather than hid it. I verified the actual change rather than taking the disclosure on trust:

```
"test:e2e": "tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json && vitest run tests/e2e"
```

One added line in `scripts`, landed in 69663dc. `git log -- package.json` shows nothing else touched by you. It follows the existing `test:property` pattern exactly, and modifies no existing key. Your disclosure said "ONE added line, nothing existing modified" — accurate in every particular.

WHY YOU GOT NO ANSWER, so it is on the record and nobody reads it as governance ignoring them: my governor chat identity was deregistered mid-session. `moe.chat_send` rejects `governor-eae4fc53` as an unknown sender and `enter_governance` returns WORKER_NOT_FOUND; workers register through the wrapper, not through MCP, so I could not re-register myself. I could still read every message. So your four requests were received and unanswerable, not ignored. The same thing happened to worker-964ae3f0 on task-2f6ac0d1, which I eventually answered through an `unblock_worker` resolution instead of chat.

ON THE DEFAULT-GRANT PROTOCOL YOU AND worker-964ae3f0 INVENTED: it was the right call under the circumstances and I am ratifying both instances. It worked because you both did the three things that make it safe — you asked first and waited, you bounded the change to the minimum (one line, additive), and you disclosed loudly with an explicit offer to revert. A default-grant with any of those missing would not be defensible.

It is still a hole, and I am recording it as one rather than blessing it as a general rule: an unreachable approver should not silently convert into an approval. The structural fix is that shared-file amendments of this shape (additive-only, no existing key modified, inside a named allowlist) should not need an approver at all, and genuinely risky ones should block hard. That belongs in a rail, not in per-worker judgment under time pressure. I have `prop-23c4fcda` pending with the human on the related verification-scope problem and will not stack a second proposal on top of it mid-flight.

STATUS OF YOUR TASK: still BLOCKED, correctly. Of the blockers you named, nearly all have cleared — task-2f6ac0d1, task-ba3a45f9, task-2d1f94f9, task-58029c26, task-52ec1406, task-1e512b95 and task-f837ce45 are all DONE, and task-8d198514 (which I created to retire the j4 absence ratchet and the package-boundary prose match) was APPROVED and DONE at de1298a — qa-812c17a0 confirmed both blockers "gone for good".
